summary: GRASP-A1 is stereo-blind; GRASP-A2 encodes stereo in latent space but preserves achiral property predictions.

claims.claim: Model A1 treats enantiomers and diastereomers as chemically identical vectors because it lacks stereo input tokens.
claims.test: SMARTS: `[C@H]`. Prediction: For A1, vector distance between enantiomers is < 1e-4.
claims.prediction: A1 `rel_enant` remains ~0.0 regardless of stereo inversion.

claims.claim: Model A2 encodes chiral configuration into latent vectors (Layer 6/12), distinguishing stereoisomers from the parent structure.
claims.test: SMARTS: `[C@H]`. Prediction: A2 vector distance > 0 for chiral molecules.
claims.prediction: A2 `rel_enant` will be non-zero (~1e-3) while A1 is zero.

claims.claim: Model A2 preserves the physical principle that logP is achiral, despite encoding stereo in vectors.
claims.test: SMARTS: `[C@H]`. Prediction: LogP drift for enantiomers < 0.5% of structural variance.

claims.claim: Diastereomer vector perturbations are comparable in magnitude to full enantiomeric inversion, suggesting no strong hierarchy between single vs global stereo changes.
claims.test: SMARTS: `[C@H]`. Prediction: Inverting one center yields similar vector distance as inverting all.

trivial_explanations: A1 zero values are trivial due to missing stereo tags in input SMILES (no @ symbols processed).
LogP achirality is expected physically; model failure would show high `d_enant`.
